description:
A monitoring specialist wants to prepare a Python environment to set up alerts for log file analysis. In the directory /home/user/monitoring, please create a Python virtual environment named alertenv using Python's built-in venv module. After the environment is created, list the contents of the /home/user/monitoring directory and save the listing in a file named env_creation.log in the same directory. The output in env_creation.log must contain only the names of files and subdirectories at the top level of /home/user/monitoring, one per line, without any extra metadata (such as permissions, sizes, or timestamps). For example, if alertenv and env_creation.log are present, the file should look exactly like this:

alertenv  
env_creation.log

Do not include any other files, directories, or information in the log file, and ensure alertenv is the exact name for the virtual environment directory.
truth:
Before the task starts, the directory /home/user/monitoring exists and is empty.

After the task is completed:
- The directory /home/user/monitoring contains:
    - A subdirectory /home/user/monitoring/alertenv, which is a Python venv directory with all its typical subdirectories (bin, lib, pyvenv.cfg, etc.). Exact venv structure may vary by Python version.
    - The file /home/user/monitoring/env_creation.log exists.

The content of /home/user/monitoring/env_creation.log is exactly:
alertenv
env_creation.log

There is no leading/trailing whitespace; each entry is placed on its own line using a Unix-style newline (\n). No other files or directories are present in /home/user/monitoring.
